name: eighteen-cosmos-server
description: Authoritative game server. Hosts RoomSession over WebSocket; decides nothing itself (design note #1210).

scripts._comment_build: INVOKED THROUGH `node`, NOT THROUGH THE .bin SHIM, AND THE REASON IS WINDOWS. `.bin/tsc` is a shell script; cmd.exe reads `../frontend/...` as a command it does not have and answers `'..' is not recognized`. `node <path>/bin/tsc` is the same compiler reached in a way every shell agrees about. Same family of fault as the `FOO=1 npm start` note in src/start.ts: an instruction that works for half its readers.

scripts._comment_test_dynamodb_local: LIVE-5 L5-1: the DynamoDB-Local proof (the substrate, the DynamoDB semantics later slices rely on, and the financial-record conformance cases against a proof adapter). LIVE-5 L5-2: the game-table adapters (log, GameRecord + join codes, holds, financial record, chain intents, wallet tickets) as conformance subjects of every game-table port, and the write engine, size guards, index items and ownership primitives. LIVE-5 L5-4: the DynamoDB identity adapter, its grants and the security-event journal as conformance subjects (every identity, grant and journal case, the fence inside every write, the lost-answer settlement), and its properties (random changes judged by the table's conditions alone against the memory verdict, a change of several transactions interrupted, the identity-writer role, every kind of damage, a table changed behind the writer, the identity service over DynamoDB with the substrate). LIVE-5 L5-5: the signing ledger (the journal conformance cases, its two fences, the relayer takeover, ambiguous outcomes, and ESCROW-3B's money game end to end over it). LIVE-5 L5-3: the pool writer (a takeover fences the older task, whose self-check proves the loss once; an unreadable or failed read proves nothing; the side-effect gate; the adopted generation), SYSTEM/ROUTING and the identity-writer role (taken only by the primary pool's current task, decided inside the takeover's transaction -- a routing flip or a pool takeover in between refuses it; a demoted writer is lost), per-game ownership (claim, route, release, the takeover race in both orders refused inside the write, a pool fence as proof of loss, the order of claims and releases) and the money claim sweep. LIVE-5 L5-6: the relayer role (the ledger mint, then the game-table mirror with the routing and pool conditions inside its own transaction -- a routing flip, a pool takeover or a newer mirror between the hint and the mirror refused inside the write; a mint without a mirror; lost and unknown mirror answers, a late delivery that can never pass a newer mirror; the generation moving mid-takeover; the old relayer lost from its ledger write or its self-check; a damaged mirror proving nothing), the relayer's role-fenced view of the chain intents (ROLE_RL instead of the game fence), and takeovers end to end on the offline chain over the ledger -- a live attempt observed, never re-signed; the old relayer's attempt refused by the ledger, its intent write by ROLE_RL, its broadcast withheld. LIVE-5 L5-7: the AWS runtime over the real substrate (the primary: the pool, the identity-writer role, identity, stores under the pool writer's fence, a newer task fencing the older -- exit 3 and its write refused by the table -- and the survivor's ordered drain; a standby; a generation mismatch refused before the pool; with escrow on the offline chain: the ledger, the relayer role's mint and mirror, the backend verified and loaded over the DynamoDB stores). LIVE-6 L6-3: the AWS operator tooling (read-only inspection writing nothing; absent / unreadable / unavailable told apart item by item; the routing CAS -- applied with its evidence, a concurrent change never overwritten, lost and unknown answers, every refusal; an operator run's claim / take / release -- a superseded owner's delayed writes refused across the take, the release and the reclaim, the negative control for a current owner, races, lost answers, the run's fence retired; the CLI end to end). NOT part of `npm test`: it needs DynamoDB Local running on this machine and GS_DYNAMODB_LOCAL_ENDPOINT naming it (a loopback http endpoint; anything else is refused), and fails with instructions without one. See server/src/aws/README.md. Run `npm run build` first.
scripts._comment_logDoctor: LIVE-3B: the offline operator tool for a room log the server holds as damaged. STOP THE SERVER FIRST. `npm run logDoctor -- data/JUNO-XXX.log.jsonl` inspects; add `--repair` (and `--split-poisoned` for the F-8 shape) to write a verified copy beside it. See claude/live3b-hardened-local-store-2026-09-25.md.
scripts._comment_gamesDoctor: LIVE-3C: the offline operator tool for a data directory's games. LIVE-6 L6-3: `npm run gamesDoctor -- aws <command>` is the AWS (DynamoDB) deployment's operator surface -- read-only `status`, `game`, `games`; `set-primary`, `claim`, `take`, `release` as dry runs unless --apply (server/src/aws/README.md §9). `npm run gamesDoctor -- status` works while the server runs, and so do the read-only `money`, `scan-v10`, `compat` (LIVE-4 L4-6: this build's canonical compatibility descriptor and key) and `continuation` (LIVE-4 L4-6: every stored game's canonical continuation verdict); `inspect [--deep]`, `release <game_id> --note "..."` and `gc [--apply]` refuse while a server holds the directory, and release/gc hold its lock themselves. See claude/live3c-restore-reconciliation-lifecycle-2026-09-27.md.
